record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.original_question: Can SU(1,1) current-algebra representations without highest or lowest weight be given a stable string-theoretic interpretation in string theory on AdS3?

evidence.quote: Highest-weight representations of the SU(1,1) current algebra are labelled by the spin j of the primary fields.
Representations without highest or lowest weight do exist. It is, however, not clear how those could be interpreted within a stable string theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bosonic string theory on AdS_3, whose worldsheet description is governed by an SL(2,R) (equivalently SU(1,1)) Wess–Zumino–Witten model. The zero-mode subalgebra sl(2,R) admits several classes of unitary representations: (i) the discrete highest-weight series D_j^+ (lowest-weight states annihilated by the lowering generator), (ii) the discrete lowest-weight series D_j^- (highest-weight states annihilated by the raising generator), (iii) the continuous principal and supplementary series, which possess neither a highest nor a lowest weight vector, and the corresponding affine SU(1,1) current-algebra modules built on each of these.

The question is the following: do the SU(1,1) affine current-algebra representations built on zero-mode representations that have neither a highest nor a lowest weight vector admit a consistent and stable interpretation as part of the physical Hilbert space of string theory on AdS_3? In particular, specify which such representations (if any) must be included so that the resulting string spectrum is unitary, free of negative-norm physical states after imposing the Virasoro constraints, closed under the operator product expansion, and yields a modular-invariant one-loop partition function.
artifact.category_tag: AdS3 string theory and SL(2,R) WZW representations
artifact.status_search_result: Maldacena and Ooguri (2000–2001) showed that a consistent, unitary, and modular-invariant spectrum for strings on AdS_3 requires including, in addition to the discrete highest/lowest-weight series, the affine modules built on the continuous (principal) series of SL(2,R) — representations without highest or lowest weight — together with all their spectral flows. This resolution has been confirmed and refined in subsequent work on spectral flow, correlation functions, and the symmetric orbifold dual, so the open issue raised about stable string-theoretic interpretation of such representations is now considered resolved.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS3 and the SL(2,R) WZW model. I: The spectrum (Maldacena–Ooguri)
status_evidence.snippet: The physical spectrum includes affine modules based on the continuous representations of SL(2,R) (no highest or lowest weight) together with their spectral-flowed images, giving a unitary, modular-invariant string spectrum on AdS_3.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous (non-highest/lowest-weight) SU(1,1) representations and their spectral flows are required and consistent in AdS_3 string theory.

status_evidence.title: Spectral flow and localisation in AdS3 string theory, JHEP 05 (2024) 113
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to use and confirm the Maldacena–Ooguri spectrum including continuous representations and spectral flow.
status_evidence.claim: The inclusion of non-highest-weight (continuous) representations with spectral flow remains the established consistent framework.
